title: AI Caricature Generator
summary: Free AI caricature generator: turn your photo into a funny caricature with a big head and small body, or try the me and my job trend. Free to try.
body_markdown:
### How do I make a caricature of myself with AI?


Add a clear, front-facing photo of yourself as a reference image, then ask for a caricature with a big head on a small body, naming the features to exaggerate and the ones to keep, such as your hair, glasses and smile.


### What is the me and my job AI caricature trend?


The me and my job trend is a caricature made from your own photo that shows you with a big head on a small body, surrounded by the tools, animals or places of your work, often shared as a profile picture or a work post.


### Is there a free AI caricature generator?


Yes. Flick is free to start: the free plan gives 100 credits every day with no credit card, and GPT Image 2.6, which made the caricatures here, costs 5 credits an image at its default settings.


### Can AI keep my face recognisable in a caricature?


Yes, when you give it a photo and ask it to exaggerate the features you already have rather than invent new ones; GPT Image 2.6 takes up to 10 reference images, so you can add more than one photo of yourself.


### What styles can an AI caricature be drawn in?


Most styles work when you name them: street fair marker sketches, watercolour, pen and ink with crosshatching, digital painting with bold outlines, gouache, clay and glossy 3D bobblehead renders.


### Can I make a caricature of a couple or a family?


Yes. Describe each person with one exaggerated feature and one action, and add a photo of each as a reference, so every face stays recognisable in the same scene.


### Can I turn a caricature into a video?


Yes. Generate the still first, then use it as the start frame of an image to video model in Flick and describe one simple action, such as a chef tossing pizza dough, and ask it to keep the big head and small body exactly as drawn.
